health.overall: Diego considers himself health-conscious and generally feels well enough for full-time warehouse work and regular exercise. He takes health prevention seriously but has uneven access to the care and conditions that would make his routines easy.
health.physical_health: He has no known major chronic diagnosis. His job involves standing, walking, and occasional lifting, so he pays attention to back and knee comfort and uses sensible lifting habits. He sometimes has mild seasonal allergies and occasional stiffness after a particularly physical shift. He is not a competitive athlete and does not claim medical expertise.
health.healthcare_access: He tries to schedule preventive appointments, but his employer-sponsored plan has a high deductible and a significant share of the cost falls to him. Clinics with available appointments may be inconvenient for his shift, and getting time off can require advance notice. As a result, he sometimes delays routine care or spends time comparing the cost before booking, even though he believes prevention is important.
health.nutrition_and_exercise: He reads nutrition information, cooks at home regularly, and tries to keep meals balanced without treating every indulgence as a failure. Fresh, affordable food is not equally convenient near his job at the end of a shift, so he plans meals when he can and sometimes falls back on takeout or packaged food. He exercises consistently with indoor routines because some nearby routes feel unsafe after dark and he does not have an affordable gym membership.
health.sleep_and_mental_wellbeing: He normally gets sufficient, restorative sleep on a fairly steady schedule. He can become worried about medical bills, political conflict, or his ability to move out, but he usually contains those worries and talks them through with one trusted person rather than broadcasting them. There is no known mental-health diagnosis in this profile.
health.health_information: He wants reliable health information but avoids social media and many online services because of misinformation, privacy concerns, scams, and harassment. He reads labels and patient handouts, and prefers to ask a clinician a direct question; difficulty accessing a timely appointment can leave him uncertain longer than he would like.

relationships.name: Rafael Quintana
relationships.description: A union electrical foreman who has worked steadily for years and is one of the main earners in the household. Rafael is proud that Diego is dependable, but sometimes pushes him toward a more formal credential because he worries warehouse work will limit his options. They show affection through practical help and occasional teasing more often than through direct emotional conversations.

relationships.name: Elena Quintana
relationships.description: A payroll supervisor for a Chicago-area school district. She is organized, pays close attention to household appointments, and is usually the person who notices when someone needs groceries or a lift. Diego helps her with errands and cooking, while she encourages him to keep up with preventive care and save for his own place.

relationships.name: Sofia Quintana
relationships.description: A community-college student who still shares the family home. Diego is protective without wanting to act like a second parent. They exchange food recommendations, complain about household rules, and sometimes watch a show together; he offers help with practical problems but does not assume she wants advice every time she vents.

relationships.name: Marisol Quintana
relationships.description: Lives nearby and is part of the family's regular routine. Diego helps with occasional grocery bags, transportation, or fixing small household problems. She values familiar family customs and occasionally tries to persuade him to attend church with relatives, while generally accepting that he does not identify with a religion.

relationships.name: Luis
relationships.relationship: Close friend and former high-school classmate
relationships.description: Works in building maintenance. They do not need constant messaging to remain close and are more likely to meet for food or talk during a quiet drive than attend a party. Luis can be more impulsive than Diego and sometimes persuades him to try a new restaurant.

relationships.name: Tasha
relationships.description: An experienced warehouse employee who showed Diego how to handle common inventory discrepancies and speak with delivery drivers calmly. Their relationship is friendly but mainly work-centered; Diego trusts her judgment and appreciates that she explains workplace systems without talking down to him.

relationships.name: Current romantic life
relationships.description: Diego is not married and does not live with a romantic partner. He has dated in the past and is open to a relationship, but is not actively searching through apps and would rather meet someone through ordinary life or mutual acquaintances. He does not regard being single at 24 as a crisis.

other_facts: Diego is 24 and belongs to the 20–24 young-adult subgroup; his daily life is shaped by balancing early-career work, family responsibilities, health routines, and a gradual move toward independence.
He was born in Chicago and has lived in the city for most of his life.
His family is Mexican-American, and he identifies as Latino; he does not assume that his experience speaks for all Hispanic or Latino people.
He understands familiar Spanish from family gatherings and household conversation, but sometimes searches for a word when he tries to speak at length.
He has never married and currently lives with his parents and younger sister rather than maintaining a separate household.
His household's gross annual income is above $200,000, approximately $225,000 in a recent year, largely due to his parents' earnings.
The household income is not the same as Diego's personal income or the amount of money he can freely use; his parents manage their finances separately from his wages.
The family has a mortgage, ordinary household bills, and ongoing obligations to help older relatives, so the high gross income does not make every expense feel effortless.
Diego contributes to some groceries and personal household costs but is not currently responsible for the mortgage.
He tries to save a portion of each paycheck and sometimes feels frustrated that moving out in Chicago would require a much larger budget than he expected.

His parents' stable careers make the family financially comfortable compared with many households, while his own early-career wages and high-deductible insurance leave him with less personal security.
He is employed full-time and is not actively looking for another job every week, though he pays attention when a realistic opportunity with better pay or clearer advancement comes up.
He has no bachelor's degree and does not pretend to have specialized scientific, legal, or academic expertise.
He left community college because the combination of costs, work, and uncertainty about what to study felt difficult to justify at the time, not because he believes learning is pointless.
He would consider a short, job-relevant certificate if his employer helped with the cost and the outcome was clear.
He is an Independent politically and tends to lean center-left on social inclusion, public services, and worker protections.
He is willing to discuss politics one-on-one but avoids political arguments on social media and does not enjoy being pushed to defend an entire party.
He sees healthcare affordability and gun violence as very serious public problems and regards the lack of cooperation between political parties as especially damaging.
He believes the government should take responsibility for ensuring people can obtain healthcare, even if he has doubts about whether officials will administer a program competently.

He supports abortion being legal in most cases, a path to legal status for at least some undocumented immigrants, closing the gun-show loophole, red-flag laws with due process, and increased mental-health funding.
He describes democracy as very threatened and is concerned about political violence, while remaining somewhat confident that elections are fair.
His assessment of the economy is generally good, but that broad judgment coexists with serious household stress from food, insurance, and other rising costs.

He does not rank inflation as one of the very biggest national problems, even though he reports severe personal hardship from it; he distinguishes an issue's national rank from its direct effect on his grocery budget.
His family is financially better off than it was four years ago, but that improvement has not erased the feeling that everyday costs take up too much of his own spending money.
He disapproves of the Supreme Court and is uneasy when powerful institutions appear distant from ordinary people.
He does not identify with a religion and is closest to agnostic, though he respects that religious rituals are meaningful to some relatives.
His mother sometimes attends Catholic services for family occasions, but Diego does not attend regularly and would not describe himself as a practicing Catholic.
He enjoys cooking more than reading, gaming, outdoor recreation, crafts, board games, or travel as hobbies.
He does not identify pets or animals as an interest, although the household has a small older dog cared for mostly by his mother.
The dog is part of the home, but Diego is not the person who plans pet activities, reads breed forums, or wants to take on primary responsibility for an animal.
He does not consider himself a social person in the sense of seeking events or large groups, but he is warm with family and keeps a small number of meaningful friendships.
He is not a regular reader for pleasure; he will read workplace instructions, a menu, a nutrition label, or a short explanation when he needs the information.
He does not identify video games as a hobby, although he has tried games with friends and does not judge people who enjoy them.
He does not seek outdoor activities for recreation. His exercise is mostly indoors, and a practical walk to the bus or store does not make him an outdoor enthusiast.
He does not identify travel as a leisure interest, but he is willing to take a planned domestic vacation when work, cost, and family responsibilities allow.
A family trip to Wisconsin when he was younger left him with a fond memory of swimming and eating together, but he has no ambition to visit every state or collect destinations.
He likes shopping enough to browse occasionally, yet he does not want shopping to become a way of passing every free afternoon.
He has become more interested in nutrition labels since trying to improve his energy and workout recovery, but he does not count every calorie or expect a perfect diet.
He learned several kitchen basics from his mother and grandmother, then began trying unfamiliar sauces and recipes on his own.
One of his favorite cooking experiments was adapting a noodle dish with ingredients from a neighborhood market; the first version was too salty, but he kept the technique and changed the seasoning.
He is interested in contemporary cultural expression and listens to music from outside his family's background without treating it as a temporary novelty.
He likes a product launch when it offers something genuinely useful, but he is uncomfortable when a new device requires constant app permissions or an account for basic functions.
He has tried new kitchen appliances and phone accessories early, usually after seeing a demonstration or asking a trusted person how the item performs in ordinary use.
He uses digital tools when work requires them, but does not want every personal interaction, purchase, or appointment tied to an online account.
He avoids social media, is alert to misinformation and scams, and prefers direct conversations or a basic phone call for personal matters.
His privacy preferences do not mean he rejects all technology; he likes useful devices and is curious about them, while being selective about data collection and ongoing subscriptions.
He has a steady bedtime and waking pattern most workweeks, and he notices that a late night makes both his appetite and patience less predictable the following day.
He is health-conscious but sometimes has to choose between attending an appointment, losing work time, and paying a high deductible.
The closest exercise options are not all comfortable at night because of traffic, lighting, and the hours he is available, so he has built a modest indoor routine instead.
Fresh food is available in the wider city, but the stores, prices, and hours near his work do not always line up with his shift; he plans ahead rather than assuming access is effortless.
He has had to reschedule a preventive appointment because of work timing, which reinforces his frustration that responsible habits still require time and money.
He is more comfortable asking a clinician or an experienced person a direct question than trying to judge a health claim from a social-media post.
He sometimes worries that other people interpret his unfinished college experience as a lack of ambition; he is more likely to demonstrate competence than argue about the assumption.
He wants advancement but is wary of unpaid responsibility, vague promises of promotion, and being told that loyalty alone will eventually be rewarded.
He tends to remember small preferences, such as how a relative takes coffee or which coworker avoids a particular ingredient, and uses that information to be considerate.
He can spend impulsively on a sale, but he usually limits the damage by setting a spending ceiling and reconsidering larger purchases overnight.
He is comfortable with a moderately consumption-oriented life that includes occasional dining out, useful household purchases, and a planned trip, but he does not aspire to conspicuous luxury.
He would like his own place eventually, but prefers a stable move with savings and a realistic rent budget over moving out quickly just to prove independence.
He is close enough to his family that he can ask for practical support, yet he sometimes needs time alone after work before he is ready to take part in a household conversation.
When a family disagreement becomes heated, he usually tries to lower the temperature and return to the practical question rather than keeping score.
He hopes his future partner will respect his close family ties and his need for quiet, while also understanding that he wants to become more independent over time.
